_readme: The global Nuvio Z changelog: one history across Desktop, Android and iOS, byte-identical in nuvio-z and
nuviozdesktop (scripts/check-changelog.py compare). The app ships it and reads it offline; the release tooling
reads it for the release body. An event is identified and ordered by `seq` (global, monotonic, unique), never by
a version, a date or one family's serial. `ships` lists only the platforms the event actually ships on, each with
its own version, release serial and date ("unreleased" until that platform's release commit sets it). Android
and iOS ship one mobile version under one serial. Events are listed newest first. category: feature |
improvement | fix; platforms: android | ios | desktop, each one a platform the event ships on. Optional:
`summary` (one line, not a name), `action` (advanced_setup), `qa` (an open acceptance item: the app ignores it,
and check-changelog.py refuses to release an event that still has one). Debug-build notes are per repository,
in changelog-debug.json. Run `python3 scripts/check-changelog.py validate` after every edit.

events.summary: The first proper Nuvio Z release on Android and iPhone, and a big update on desktop: downloads rebuilt from the ground up, Advanced Setup, and Watch Together parties that now include phones.

entries.title: Nuvio Z, on your phone
entries.body: This is the first proper Nuvio Z release for Android and iPhone, built from the same code as the desktop app. It has the three playback modes, the new Downloads, Social and Watch Together, all covered below. Android keeps itself up to date from inside the app; on iPhone, Nuvio Z installs and updates through SideStore.

entries.title: Watch Together, on every screen
entries.body: Start a party from anything you're playing and watch in sync with friends, on any mix of desktop, Android and iPhone. Everyone plays the same release through their own sources, so nobody shares an account or a link. The host can keep control or share it, invite friends or hand out a code, and decide who can join: Direct, Ask or Off. When the host moves on to the next episode, the whole party comes along. On a phone, Watch Together is in the player's toolbar and in the ⋯ menu next to Play. On iPhone, the lock screen and headphone controls go through the party too.
entries.qa: Physical iPhone Watch Together acceptance (lock, Away, return) is still open on the RC.

entries.title: Away, instead of "buffering"
entries.body: If someone switches apps or locks their phone mid-party, they now show as Away rather than looking like a stalled stream. The host can choose to wait for them with Pause for away users in the Watch Together panel, separate from Pause when someone buffers. When they come back, they catch up before the party carries on. Clicking into another window on desktop doesn't count as leaving.
entries.qa: Physical iPhone Watch Together acceptance (lock, Away, return) is still open on the RC.

entries.title: Social
entries.body: Add friends by their handle, see what they're Watching Now and what they've Recently Watched on Home and in the Social tab, and ask to join with one tap. You choose whether friends see what you're watching, what you've finished, or neither. Social is optional: turn it off during setup or in Settings → Social, and the tab, the activity rows and Watch Together disappear. Nothing is deleted; switching it back on brings everything back.

entries.title: Three ways to press play
entries.body: Classic shows every source and lets you choose. Streamlined asks one question, what quality you want, and picks the best release in it. Instant asks nothing: it checks your connection, picks what it can actually carry and tells you what it opened, with a Change button if you disagree. It asks once before using mobile data. Long-press any episode to get the full source list whatever your mode. Pick a mode in Settings → Playback.

entries.title: A quality picker built from what's really there
entries.body: The picker is built from the releases a title actually has: one row per resolution, quality bands that mean the same thing on every title, and the connection speed each choice needs, measured from the source rather than guessed. One set of ranking rules sits behind it. CAM and TS copies, AI-upscaled "8K" and oversized season packs stop floating to the top, and a debrid source that isn't cached is never picked for you.

entries.title: A loading screen that says what it's doing
entries.body: From the moment you pick a source to the first frame, one screen shows what's happening (finding sources, checking the connection, resolving the link, starting playback) and five facts about the file: resolution, languages, HDR, audio and size. If a source dies, the next one is tried on the same screen ("Attempt 2 of 3"). If nothing works, you land back on the source list with the reason, and Choose source manually appears after a few seconds.

entries.title: Downloads have their own mode
entries.body: Download Mode is now separate from how playback works. Automatic picks the file for you under your rules and asks only when it has to. Assisted asks what quality you want and finds the best matching file. Manual lets you pick the exact file, and choosing one never starts playback by accident. Change it in Settings → Downloads. On desktop, setup asks you two quick questions about downloads the first time you open this version.

entries.title: Download preferences
entries.body: Pick a preferred resolution, a file size level and what to do when that resolution isn't available. Levels run Small, Standard, Large, Huge and Any size, each showing its GB per hour at 1080p and 4K, so you know what a season will cost your disk before it starts. They replace download presets; on desktop, your last preset carries over.

entries.title: A new Downloads screen
entries.body: Everything in one place, with artwork. A season is one row you can expand, pause or move in the queue. A single Needs you list says what's wrong and offers the fix: Allow, Use nearest, Check again, Free up space or Choose sources. It also shows how much space downloads take and offers to clear episodes you've already watched. On phones it lives under Library. On desktop it's back as its own destination in the sidebar and top bar, with the queue and your library side by side while things download.

entries.title: Your downloads, as a library that works offline
entries.body: Downloaded titles show up as cards with their artwork and a play button for what's next. A downloaded show gets its own page, with seasons as tabs and every episode ready to play. If Nuvio says a title is downloaded, it plays with no connection at all: offline playback never reaches for the internet, autoplay moves through the episodes you have, and Home tells you when you're offline. Getting on a plane should be slightly less stressful now.
entries.qa: iOS current-head download acceptance (transfer, lock/relaunch, offline playback) is still open on the RC.

entries.title: Whole seasons, without the busywork
entries.body: Download a season from a title's page, either everything or only what you haven't watched. In Assisted, its sources are found in the background: leave the screen, and Downloads tells you when it's ready for you to pick a quality, or choose now from size estimates. In Manual, one list covers the whole season: pick a source for each episode, or let Nuvio auto-pick the rest.

entries.title: Advanced Setup
entries.body: An optional guided tour of everything Initial Setup doesn't ask: the player, skipping, subtitles, posters, Home, the detail page, the source list, Social and more. Every panel has a live preview drawn from the real app, and every change applies straight away and stays in Settings. Open it any time from Settings → Setup & about.

entries.title: Setup that shows you what it changes
entries.body: The first launch walks you through what matters before what Nuvio looks like: playback mode, downloads, language, sources and Social. Each question shows the part of the app it changes, right above the controls. If you haven't added any sources yet, it can set up a recommended AIOStreams + TorBox source for you. Run it again any time from Settings → Setup & about.

entries.title: Your preferences come with you
entries.body: Sign in on a different kind of device, a phone after a computer or the other way round, and Nuvio brings your profile's preferences over. It shows a short Welcome back summary and asks only what belongs to that device, like its navigation style and player controls.

entries.title: Picture-in-Picture
entries.body: Pop the player out into a small window that stays on top while you do something else, then put it back. It's the same playback, not a second copy, and Watch Together keeps working. Windows and macOS.

entries.title: Choose your navigation
entries.body: Phones get the new floating navigation bar: adaptive, always expanded, always compact, or the classic bar, with an optional glow on Android 13 and later and the Liquid Glass tab bar on iOS 26. Desktop gets the new top bar or can keep the sidebar, and both now include Downloads and Social. Find it in Settings → Navigation.

entries.title: MDBList tracking and library
entries.body: Connect MDBList to keep your watched history and progress in sync, use it as your library, and see Rotten Tomatoes scores next to the other ratings. Settings → Integrations → MDBList Ratings.

entries.title: Shuffle
entries.body: Play a series in random order, from unwatched or all episodes. It's off by default: turn it on in Settings → Appearance → Detail Page, then press Shuffle on a show's page.

entries.title: Custom poster images (advanced)
entries.body: Point Nuvio at a poster service with a URL pattern and pick which screens use it. Titles the service doesn't cover keep their normal poster. Settings → Appearance → Poster Card Style, with Show advanced settings turned on.

entries.title: A reorganised Settings
entries.body: Settings is grouped by what you're doing: Watching, Look & feel, Content & services, Profile & social, and Setup & about. Navigation and About have their own pages, and Trakt and Simkl sit with the other integrations.

entries.title: Your codec, HDR and language choices shape playback
entries.body: Preferred codec, dynamic range and audio language decide what Streamlined and Instant pick, not just what gets downloaded, and your language choice means the same thing to the source picker and the player. Prefer built-in subtitles favours releases that carry subtitles inside the file. Leave them on Automatic and nothing changes.

entries.title: Watch Together keeps better time
entries.body: A host whose link refreshes, or who lands on the same release again, no longer drags the party anywhere; only a genuinely different release moves everyone. After a seek, the party waits until everyone has actually landed and is ready, then resumes together. Keeping a guest in sync no longer shows up as a changed playback speed.

entries.title: Smoother next episode
entries.body: When an episode ends, the next one is found in the background behind a countdown you can cancel, and the screen stays covered until it's actually playing. Pressing Next twice won't start it twice.

entries.title: New player controls
entries.body: The newer Nuvio control layout, with Watch Together in the toolbar. Prefer the old one? Settings → Playback → Legacy layout.

entries.title: Skip the credits
entries.body: Movies can now skip their end credits, or jump straight to a post-credits scene when there is one. On Android and iPhone, intros and recaps are skippable too, where they're known.

entries.title: Your subtitle choice carries to the next episode
entries.body: Pick a subtitle and the next episode picks the same one again, from the same provider and in the same language, instead of falling back to your default. Subtitles off stays off.

entries.title: Richer title details, out of the box
entries.body: Cast photos, artwork, episode details and collections come from TMDB by default, using Nuvio's built-in key. A personal key still works, each part can be switched off, and if you'd already made a choice it's kept.

entries.title: Downloads keep going when you switch profile
entries.body: One queue for the device; each profile still only sees its own downloads.

entries.title: Downloads are sorted into folders
entries.body: Each title gets its own folder with one per season, and episodes are named like "S01E01 - Pilot". On desktop, existing downloads move there the next time Nuvio starts.

entries.title: Downloads and mobile data
entries.body: Downloads wait for Wi-Fi by default. Choose Ask or Always in Settings → Downloads, or tap Download now anyway on a waiting episode.

entries.title: Downloads keep going on a locked iPhone
entries.body: Nuvio hands up to 30 downloads to iOS while it's open, so a whole season keeps downloading with the screen locked, with progress in a Live Activity. Queue more than that and the rest start the next time you open Nuvio.
entries.qa: iOS current-head download acceptance (transfer, lock/relaunch, offline playback) is still open on the RC.

entries.title: Download notifications
entries.body: One notification for progress, with Pause all and Resume, and a separate one when a title or season finishes. Assisted seasons tell you when they're ready for you to pick a quality.

entries.title: Choose how many downloads run at once
entries.body: From one to four, in Settings → Downloads.

entries.title: Settings that stay put
entries.body: More of your settings reach your other devices. Signing out removes the account's data but keeps this device's own preferences.

entries.title: What's New is one changelog now
entries.body: Updates are listed by date and show which versions shipped on which device, so notes from your other devices turn up here too, set apart at the end. Skip a few updates and this screen catches you up on everything you missed.

entries.title: Polish
entries.body: A smoother Home banner that no longer flashes through every title on its way back to the first. Refreshed dialogs, sheets and menus. A gentle shimmer in the source list while add-ons are still answering.

entries.title: Smaller desktop additions
entries.body: Fullscreen trailers, controls for which ratings are shown, and a full-window title bar on macOS.

entries.title: Also from Nuvio
entries.body: Recent searches (switch them off in Settings → Sources & addons), fullscreen trailers, controls for which ratings are shown, signing in with a link or code, stripping sound descriptions from subtitles, and gradient custom themes.

entries.title: Downloads no longer restart every minute
entries.body: Downloads from a debrid service were cut and resumed about once a minute, showing "Retrying shortly" each time. They now run straight through.

entries.title: Social reconnects by itself
entries.body: After sleep or a dropped connection, Social could say to sign in, or show "JWT expired", until you restarted. It now recovers on its own.

entries.title: An expired sign-in no longer signs you out
entries.body: A sign-in that had only expired, usually in the first seconds after waking the computer, was treated as a deleted account. It's now refreshed instead.

entries.title: Nuvio Z keeps its own sign-in
entries.body: Nuvio Z, Nuvio Z Debug and Nuvio shared one saved sign-in on Windows, so using two of them could sign all of them out. Each now keeps its own. After this update the first one you open stays signed in; any other may ask you to sign in once.

entries.title: More dependable sign-in and sign-out
entries.body: Signing in, signing out and switching accounts were reworked so a slow or failed attempt can't override a newer one.
entries.qa: Auth smoke on desktop and iOS (Android where practical) is still open on the RC.

entries.title: Watch Together fixes
entries.body: A guest following a buffering pause no longer ends it early for everyone. A party waiting to start can no longer keep a dead source alive. Starting a party on a release with lots of audio languages works, and a refused source shows a readable message instead of server text. Background party connections stay signed in for longer.

entries.title: The Download button is back on wide windows
entries.body: A title's page lost its Download button on windows 1000 dp and wider.

entries.title: Settings only shows what applies
entries.body: Desktop no longer lists the Android-only player engine options.

entries.title: Smaller fixes from Nuvio Desktop
entries.body: Recent searches no longer disappear when clicked, the pause overlay setting is respected, animated collection images play, volume changes are immediate on macOS, the poster right-click menu is back, and Discord keeps showing what you're watching.
